name: 1735 Indiana Avenue — Frame house (district draft; refined by T-1946)

function.note: The 1911 sheet draws a photographic-supply factory at 1727-1737, permitted in August 1905. T-3068 stands the plate's corner frame house for 1904 (frontage-20w-1727–1737, backcast_1886); the Tribune let rooms in it, '1735 Indiana-av., corner Eighteenth-st.', from 1888 to 1893. Its survival to 1904 is inferred: no dated sign of it after 1893 is in hand, and none of its removal before the 1905 permit.

research_note: A DISTRICT DRAFT (T-3068, the owner's district pass of 2026-10-08): a serviceable first model, complete from the street, the walks, the alley and the air, that T-1946 refines in place under this same id. Written by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py from the Robinson 1886 plate 10 reading (r1886-1735-f: the outline in the plate's pixels, carried by its T-1250 fit) (r1886-1735-f), the T-3019 census (r1886-1735-f) and the T-1837 register row frontage-20w-1727–1737 (Frame house); every height, roof, opening and feature is the draft rules' reconstruction (data/components/prairie_1904/draft_prairie_1904.json; liberty L-draft-indiana-1904-lots-3068).

documented_range.note: The draft claims the 1904 target and no more, on the plate and the 1905 permit; the house's survival to 1904 is inferred, not attested.

position.note: The rear corner of the main body's rectangle (lot frame u 26.750, v -1.750 m from the middle of the rear lot line), through the T-1250 fit of the plate: the plate's fit is 4.54 m RMS, the weakest of the four T-1250 fits (a photographed atlas page, rotated and curved toward the binding), plus about a pixel (0.35 m) of reading. Rotation 179.391 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.

derivation.reason: The four derivation methods re-derive from the 1835 files; this position is re-derived from the traced sheet and the 1904 parcel by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py --check instead.

footprint.note: The main body: the largest rectangle that fits inside the traced main part (u toward the street, v along the front). The building's other rectangles are in draft_plan.

stories.note: RECONSTRUCTED: Robinson's atlas prints no storey count and no source describes the corner house; two storeys is its neighbour's, the frame house at 1727 that the Tribune let in 1883 as two storeys over a basement.

construction.note: Robinson 1886 colours the building yellow, the plate's frame (its brick buildings are pink).
